Establishing a 96 well-based resting-cell bioconversion platform and screening first-round HACS variants. (A) GA production from formaldehyde and formate via formate activation enzyme (AbfT) and HACS. A previously demonstrated pathway (Chou et al., 2019) for formaldehyde-to-GA bioconversion with HACS, ACR, and ALDH are shown in light gray. (B) HACS and AbfT are expressed under independently inducible promoters: HACS expressed under the IPTG-inducible T7 promoter and AbfT under the cumate-inducible T5 promoter. (C) Bioconversion platform was scaled down from a shake flask (5–10 mL) to a 96-deep-well microtiter plate (1 mL) for improved throughput. (D) First-round HACS variants organized in a phylogenetic tree diagram with a heatmap diagram representing the GA flux. Node and subclades that branch out RuHACS, ApbHACS, and DhcHACS are highlighted in dark green. Variants highlighted in bold represent the selected variants as a reference for the second-round bioprospecting. Branches and leaves that belong to the OXC cluster are highlighted in red.
